newsitem.title: CHINA: China TV to air Hong Kong handover-related events.
newsitem.headline: China TV to air Hong Kong handover-related events.

text.p: China's state television will feed the world a steady diet of news and documentaries on the return of the British colony of Hong Kong to Chinese rule, television officials said on Wednesday.

For 72 hours from 6.00 a.m. (2200 GMT) on June 30, Chinese-language channels of China Central Television (CCTV) will broadcast handover-related news, documentaries and reports on celebrations and other events in Hong Kong and across China.

It will use satellite transmission to give the world a chance to see the festivities linked to Hong Kong's return to Chinese sovereignty at midnight on June 30 and the end of more than 150 years of British rule.
CCTV's English-language channel will provide similar broadcasts for 41 hours from 6.55 a.m. (2255 GMT) on June 30, the officials said.
"The audience...will be given an insight into Hong Kong's yesterday, today and tomorrow," Li Dongsheng of CCTV told reporters.

CCTV will send a 289-strong crew to Hong Kong to cover the handover ceremony, the raising of the red five-star Chinese national flag, People's Liberation Army troops marching into the territory and Governor Chris Patten's departure, the officials said.
